Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to propagating Monstera deliciosa from a viable cutting, including node identification, water and compost methods, and realistic expectations. Keep all source names and evidence identifiers out of reader-facing prose. Use only directly supported claims: do not say nodes are subtle, do not instruct readers to rotate stems, and do not diagnose leaf curling or drooping as water loss. Explain only that a viable cutting requires a node. For water propagation, ensure every instruction and image brief shows at least one node below the water line while foliage remains above it.

items.assignment: Prepare an evidence-led UK article explaining why Monstera deliciosa leaves may not develop splits, considering maturity, light, support and general growing conditions. Keep all source names and evidence identifiers out of reader-facing prose. Omit unsupported support-installation details and bespoke diagnostic signs; use only claims directly supported by the evidence pack and soften uncertain advice.

Prepare a carefully sourced UK article about Monstera deliciosa and pet safety, using authoritative veterinary or poison-control evidence and avoiding diagnosis or treatment advice. Keep all organisation names, source names and evidence identifiers out of reader-facing prose. Limit immediate advice to the directly supported instruction to contact a veterinary practice or poison service promptly. Omit unsupported handling, transport, pet-behaviour, placement and pruning-waste scenarios; use only claims directly supported by the evidence pack. Do not discuss seasonal timing, plant condition or animal behaviour as risk predictors. Do not explain how a professional decides whether attendance is needed. Do not characterise the scope of linked articles; simply provide relevant internal links where useful. Do not tell readers to confirm plant identity before contacting help. Do not name or compare professional-only and owner-facing poison services, and never refer to supplied information or the evidence pack. Describe Monstera only as not pet-safe or toxic where supported; do not call it unsuitable.
